instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Residential renovation and energy retrofit company performing deep energy upgrades including external insulation, heat pump installation, and solar PV integration. Completing ~80 projects per year. Seeking to standardize energy audit workflows with tablet-based inspection and automated grant application filing. Operate from 2-3 locations or departments. We have some budget headroom for experimentation but look for quick wins that can demonstrate value within 6 months before committing to longer-term programs. The leadership team is aligned on the need to modernize but debates where to start.
answers.pastInitiatives: Our engineering team adopted an agile methodology last year, moving from waterfall-style quarterly releases to 2-week sprints with continuous deployment. This reduced our release cycle time by 60% and improved cross-functional collaboration. However, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are still adapting to the faster cadence.
answers.strategicGoals: Our industry is facing structural decline due to technological disruption and changing consumer behavior. We cannot rely on incremental improvements to our legacy business — we need to identify entirely new value propositions that leverage our brand, customer relationships, or operational capabilities in adjacent spaces where demand is growing, not shrinking.
answers.teamSize: We have a small technology team of 4-6 people including developers, a part-time DevOps engineer, and a product manager who also handles project management. The team is fully allocated to maintaining current products and handling integration requests from key clients. Innovation work is done in the margins — there is no formally ring-fenced innovation time or budget.

input.changes_since_last: Acquired 8 new enterprise clients. Expanded into adjacent market. Digital maturity improving.

opportunities.title: Standardizing Audit Workflows for Scale and Efficiency
opportunities.rationale: The core business (energy retrofits) is ripe for process standardization. Implementing tablet-based inspection and automated filing will reduce manual labor, improve data quality, and allow the company to handle larger project volumes efficiently. This directly addresses their need for quick wins.

first_actions: Map current audit workflow end-to-end (pre-tech solution).
Select off-the-shelf tablet/field inspection app platform (e.g., Fulcrum, KoboToolbox).
Pilot the digital workflow on 2 small projects to test user adoption and data capture.
Develop automated report templates linked to the digital inputs.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in audit preparation time per project by 25%.
milestones: Pilot testing successful on the first 5 projects.
Integration with existing CRM/billing system confirmed.

opportunities.title: Developing Adjacent Service Offerings through Value Stream Mapping
opportunities.rationale: The company explicitly needs to move beyond incremental improvements into new value propositions. Leveraging their existing customer relationships and deep technical knowledge (heat pumps, solar PV) allows them to explore adjacent markets like building energy consulting or residential asset management, moving up the value chain.

first_actions: Conduct structured interviews with 5-10 enterprise clients about their future needs beyond renovation.
Develop a 'consulting snapshot' service offering based on initial insights (low commitment).
Partner with an architectural/engineering firm to co-develop the new service line.
Create a simple internal knowledge base repository (using Agile principles) for gathered market data.
resources_needed: Leadership time dedicated to strategy (5 hours/week)
Small budget for external consulting insights
execution_plan.success_metric: Identification and validation of 2 high-potential adjacent service lines.
milestones: Initial client needs analysis report delivered in 6 weeks.
Drafted value proposition (VPD) presented to the team.
Formalized partnership agreement with an external expert.

next_steps.action: Formalize ring-fenced time/budget for innovation leadership (minimum 4 hours per week).
Implement an internal 'Pain Point' hackathon/workshop focused on breaking down operational silos between engineering, marketing, and support.
Develop a clear market entry hypothesis for the top adjacent service opportunity identified in opp_2, including pricing models.

key_weaknesses: Lack of formal, dedicated time or budget for innovation activities (Innovation is done in the margins).
Process silos persist despite Agile adoption; non-engineering teams are lagging in adopting fast change cadences.
Strategy formulation is diffuse; leadership is aligned on the need to modernize but lacks clear consensus on a starting point.

improvements: Improved operational speed and collaboration within the engineering department via Agile adoption (60% reduction in release cycle time).
Increased market presence and stability due to acquiring 8 new enterprise clients.
Internal technical capabilities are strengthening, evidenced by DevOps practices.
persistent_gaps: Cross-departmental process standardization is incomplete (marketing/support gap).
Strategic focus remains reactive/incremental rather than proactively defining future market positioning.
Operational scaling remains constrained by manual data handling and workflow bottlenecks in the field.
achieved_milestones: Successfully implemented 2-week sprint cycles for core product development.
Secured multiple new high-value enterprise accounts.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Significant operational improvement (Agile adoption) and market success (8 new enterprise clients). The focus has shifted from internal process refinement to external strategic growth and deep workflow digitalization.
